lessons.title: Using High Tunnels and Greenhouses
lessons.body: A high tunnel is a simple, unheated greenhouse made of metal hoops covered with clear plastic. It protects tomatoes from rain, wind, and cold, and can extend your growing season by 4 to 8 weeks in spring and fall. In Africa, high tunnels are used in Kenya, South Africa, and Ethiopia to grow tomatoes year-round. You can build a low-cost high tunnel using locally available materials: wooden or metal poles spaced 2 meters apart, bent into arches, and covered with 6-mil UV-treated polyethylene plastic. The tunnel should be 2.5 to 3 meters high at the center and 4 to 6 meters wide. Orient the tunnel east-west to capture maximum sunlight. Ventilation is critical: roll up the sides during the day when temperatures exceed 25Â°C, and close them at night. Without ventilation, temperatures inside can reach 40Â°C or more, which will kill your tomatoes. Install a thermometer at plant level to monitor. In hot climates, use shade cloth (30-50% shade) over the plastic during peak summer. For cold climates, add a second layer of plastic or a thermal screen at night. High tunnels also reduce fungal diseases because leaves stay dry. However, they require careful water management: drip irrigation is best to avoid wet foliage. You can grow tomatoes in the ground or in containers. In sandy soils, add compost to improve water holding. A well-managed high tunnel can produce 8 to 10 kg of tomatoes per square meter per season, compared to 4 to 6 kg in open fields. Start with a small tunnel (e.g., 6m x 10m) to learn, then expand. Remember to secure the plastic tightly to withstand wind, and replace it every 3-4 years when it becomes cloudy and less transparent.

lessons.title: Heating and Cooling Systems for Tomatoes
lessons.body: Tomatoes grow best between 18Â°C and 26Â°C during the day and 15Â°C to 20Â°C at night. Temperatures below 10Â°C or above 35Â°C stop fruit set. In cold climates, you need heating; in hot climates, you need cooling. For heating, the cheapest method is a compost pile inside the greenhouse: decomposing manure and straw release heat. You can also use a wood stove, but ensure proper ventilation to avoid carbon monoxide. In South Africa, some farmers use solar water heaters connected to pipes under the soil to warm the root zone. For small tunnels, use row covers or thermal blankets at night. In hot climates, cooling is more common. Use shade nets (50-70% shade) to reduce sunlight intensity. Install roll-up sides and roof vents to allow hot air to escape. A simple evaporative cooling system uses a fan pulling air through a wet pad; this can lower temperature by 5-10Â°C. In dry areas like the Sahel, this is very effective. You can also mist the roof with water. Monitor temperature with a max-min thermometer. For tomatoes, avoid sudden temperature swings; they cause fruit cracking. In winter, if you heat, keep night temperature above 15Â°C. In summer, if you cool, keep day temperature below 30Â°C. Use a thermostat to control heaters and fans automatically. In Africa, many farmers use passive systems: whitewashing the plastic with lime to reflect heat, or opening vents manually. A simple rule: if you are comfortable in a t-shirt, your tomatoes are likely fine. If you are sweating, they are too hot; if you need a jacket, they are too cold.

lessons.title: Managing Humidity and Ventilation
lessons.body: High humidity in a greenhouse encourages fungal diseases like late blight and leaf mold. Tomatoes prefer relative humidity (RH) between 60% and 70%. Above 85% RH, pollination is poor and leaves stay wet. Below 50% RH, plants lose too much water and flowers dry out. To manage humidity, ventilate. Open vents and roll-up sides in the morning to let moist air out. In cool climates, heat the greenhouse slightly to increase the air's water-holding capacity. In hot climates, use fans to circulate air. A simple hygrometer measures RH; they are cheap and available at farm supply shops. Avoid overhead watering; use drip irrigation to keep foliage dry. Water in the morning so any splashed water evaporates by evening. Mulch with straw or plastic to reduce evaporation from the soil. If you see condensation on the inside of the plastic in the morning, humidity is too high; increase ventilation. In Africa, many greenhouses have roll-up sides that can be adjusted throughout the day. A good practice is to open vents when inside temperature reaches 25Â°C, even if humidity is low, to prevent heat buildup. At night, close vents to conserve heat. In humid tropical regions, consider using a dehumidifier or a solar-powered fan. For small tunnels, simply lifting the plastic during the day is enough. Watch for disease: if you see white fuzzy mold on leaves, increase ventilation immediately and remove affected leaves. Also, avoid crowding plants; space them 40-50 cm apart to allow air movement. Proper ventilation also helps with pollination: gentle air movement shakes the flowers, aiding self-pollination. Without ventilation, fruit set can drop by 30%.

lessons.title: Hydroponic and Container Tomato Production
lessons.body: Hydroponics means growing tomatoes in water with dissolved nutrients, without soil. It saves water (up to 80% less) and allows precise control. In Africa, hydroponics is used in urban areas and dry regions. The simplest system is the bucket system: a 20-liter bucket filled with a nutrient solution, with a net pot on top holding a tomato seedling in perlite or coco peat. An air pump (like for aquariums) oxygenates the solution. Change the solution every 2 weeks. For larger scale, use Dutch buckets or NFT (nutrient film technique) channels. Nutrient solution: use a balanced tomato fertilizer (e.g., NPK 4-18-38) at 2 grams per liter of water. Adjust pH to 5.8-6.2 using pH down (phosphoric acid) or pH up (potassium hydroxide). Check with a pH meter. EC (electrical conductivity) should be 2.0-3.5 mS/cm. Start with 2.0 for seedlings and increase to 3.5 for fruiting. In hot climates, keep the solution cool (below 25Â°C) by burying the reservoir or adding ice bottles. Container growing is easier: use 20-30 liter pots filled with a mix of compost, coco peat, and perlite. Water daily, and feed with a liquid fertilizer every week. Tomatoes in containers need support: use a stake or trellis. Choose determinate varieties (like 'Roma') for containers because they stay compact. In Africa, you can use old buckets, tires, or sacks. Ensure drainage holes. Hydroponics and containers allow you to grow tomatoes on a balcony, rooftop, or small plot. They also avoid soil-borne diseases. However, they require daily attention: check water level, pH, and EC. A power outage can kill plants in a few hours if the air pump stops. Have a backup battery. With good management, you can harvest 5-8 kg per plant per season.

lessons.title: Extending the Growing Season with Row Covers
lessons.body: Row covers are lightweight fabrics or plastic sheets placed directly over plants or on low hoops. They protect tomatoes from frost, wind, insects, and even intense sun. In Africa, row covers are used in highlands to extend the season. There are two main types: floating row covers (spunbonded polypropylene) and plastic tunnels (low hoops with slitted plastic). Floating row covers are very light (17-30 g/mÂ²) and can be laid directly on plants; they allow light, air, and water through. They give 2-4Â°C of frost protection. Use them in early spring to warm the soil and protect seedlings. Remove them when plants start to flower, because pollinators need access. For tomatoes, you can also use them to exclude pests like whiteflies and aphids, reducing virus transmission. Low tunnels use hoops (e.g., 9-gauge wire) covered with clear plastic. You can open the ends for ventilation. These give 4-8Â°C of frost protection and can advance harvest by 2-3 weeks. In cold climates, use double layers. In hot climates, use shade cloth row covers (30-50% shade) to reduce heat stress. Row covers are cheap: a 10-meter roll of floating row cover costs about $10-20 and can be reused for 2-3 seasons. To install, place hoops every 1-1.5 meters, cover with fabric, and secure edges with soil or sandbags. On windy days, ensure covers are tight. Monitor temperature under covers: on sunny days, it can get 10Â°C hotter than outside, so vent by lifting sides. Remove covers when plants are too tall or when temperatures are consistently above 20Â°C. Row covers are a simple, low-cost way to get earlier tomatoes and protect against unexpected cold snaps.

lessons.title: Winter Production in Cold Climates
lessons.body: In cold climates, winter tomato production requires a heated greenhouse or a very well-insulated high tunnel. In Africa, this applies to high-altitude areas like the Ethiopian Highlands, Lesotho, and the Drakensberg. Temperatures can drop below 0Â°C at night. To grow tomatoes in winter, you need to maintain at least 15Â°C at night and 20Â°C during the day. Use a double-layer greenhouse with an air gap for insulation. Add a thermal screen (aluminized fabric) that you pull over plants at night to reduce heat loss by 30-40%. Heating options: wood stove, paraffin heater, or solar-powered electric heater. In South Africa, some farmers use geothermal heat from hot springs. But the most practical for small-scale is a compost heap inside the greenhouse: a pile of manure and straw (1m x 1m x 1m) generates heat for several weeks. You can also bury pipes in the soil and circulate warm water from a solar water heater. Choose cold-tolerant tomato varieties like 'Sub Arctic Plenty' or 'Siberian'. These set fruit at lower temperatures. Start seeds indoors in late summer. Plant in the greenhouse in early autumn. Use black plastic mulch to warm the soil. Water sparingly in winter; excess moisture causes root rot. Ventilate briefly on sunny days to reduce humidity, but avoid losing heat. Expect slower growth: fruit may take 3-4 months to mature. Yields will be lower than summer, maybe 3-4 kg per plant. But winter tomatoes fetch high prices. In Lesotho, farmers use 'passive solar greenhouses' made of stone walls and plastic, which store heat during the day and release it at night. These can keep tomatoes alive through light frosts. Always have a backup plan: if a severe cold snap is coming, harvest mature green tomatoes and ripen them indoors.

quiz.q: What is the main purpose of a high tunnel?
options: A) To provide heat for winter production
B) To protect plants from rain, wind, and cold
quiz.explanation: High tunnels are unheated structures that protect crops from adverse weather and extend the season.

quiz.q: What is the recommended orientation for a high tunnel in Africa?
quiz.explanation: East-west orientation captures maximum sunlight throughout the day.

quiz.q: Why is ventilation important in a high tunnel?
options: A) To reduce humidity and prevent overheating
quiz.explanation: Ventilation prevents temperatures from exceeding 40Â°C and reduces fungal diseases by lowering humidity.

quiz.q: What is the ideal daytime temperature range for tomatoes?
quiz.explanation: Tomatoes grow best between 18Â°C and 26Â°C during the day.

quiz.q: Which method can be used to heat a greenhouse cheaply?
quiz.explanation: Decomposing manure and straw release heat, providing a low-cost heating method.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of shade nets in hot climates?
quiz.explanation: Shade nets reduce light intensity and lower temperature, preventing heat stress.

quiz.q: What relative humidity range is ideal for tomatoes?
quiz.explanation: Tomatoes prefer 60-70% relative humidity; higher encourages disease, lower causes water stress.

quiz.q: How can you reduce humidity in a greenhouse?
options: B) Open vents and roll-up sides
quiz.explanation: Ventilation allows moist air to escape, lowering humidity.

quiz.q: Why is drip irrigation preferred in greenhouses?
quiz.explanation: Drip irrigation delivers water to roots without wetting leaves, reducing disease.

quiz.q: What is a sign that humidity is too high in a greenhouse?
options: A) Condensation on the inside of the plastic
quiz.explanation: Condensation in the morning indicates high humidity, requiring increased ventilation.

quiz.q: What is hydroponics?
options: B) Growing plants in water with nutrients
quiz.explanation: Hydroponics is growing plants in a nutrient solution without soil.

quiz.q: What is the ideal pH range for hydroponic tomatoes?
quiz.explanation: Tomatoes in hydroponics need a slightly acidic pH of 5.8-6.2 for nutrient uptake.

quiz.q: What does EC measure in hydroponics?
quiz.explanation: EC (electrical conductivity) indicates the concentration of dissolved nutrients.

quiz.q: Why are determinate tomato varieties good for containers?
quiz.explanation: Determinate varieties have a bushy, compact growth habit suitable for containers.

quiz.q: What is a common container size for tomato plants?
quiz.explanation: Tomatoes need ample root space; 20-30 liter containers are recommended.

quiz.q: What is a floating row cover?
options: A) A plastic sheet on hoops
B) A lightweight fabric laid over plants
quiz.explanation: Floating row covers are lightweight fabrics that rest directly on plants.

quiz.q: How much frost protection do floating row covers provide?
quiz.explanation: Floating row covers typically provide 2-4Â°C of frost protection.

quiz.q: When should you remove floating row covers from tomatoes?
options: B) When plants are 10 cm tall
quiz.explanation: Remove covers at flowering to allow pollinators access.

quiz.q: What is a benefit of using row covers in pest management?
options: B) They exclude pests like whiteflies
quiz.explanation: Row covers act as a physical barrier, reducing pest infestation and virus transmission.

quiz.q: What is the main challenge of winter tomato production in cold climates?
quiz.explanation: Cold temperatures below 10Â°C stop fruit set and growth, requiring heating.

quiz.q: What temperature should be maintained at night for winter tomatoes?
quiz.explanation: Night temperature should be at least 15Â°C for fruit set and growth.

quiz.q: What is a thermal screen?
options: B) An aluminized fabric pulled over plants at night
quiz.explanation: Thermal screens reduce heat loss by 30-40% at night.

quiz.q: Which tomato variety is cold-tolerant?
quiz.explanation: Sub Arctic Plenty is bred to set fruit at lower temperatures.

quiz.q: What is a passive solar greenhouse?
options: A) A greenhouse with electric heaters
B) A greenhouse that stores heat in stone walls
C) A greenhouse with no cover
quiz.explanation: Passive solar greenhouses use thermal mass (e.g., stone walls) to store heat during the day and release it at night.

quiz.q: Why should you avoid overhead watering in a greenhouse?
quiz.explanation: Wet foliage encourages fungal diseases like late blight.

quiz.q: What is the recommended spacing for tomato plants in a greenhouse?
quiz.explanation: Spacing of 40-50 cm allows air movement and reduces disease.

quiz.q: What is the role of an air pump in a bucket hydroponic system?
options: B) To oxygenate the nutrient solution
quiz.explanation: Air pumps oxygenate the solution, preventing root rot.

quiz.q: What is the EC range for fruiting tomatoes in hydroponics?
quiz.explanation: Fruiting tomatoes require higher nutrient concentration, EC 2.0-3.5 mS/cm.

quiz.q: What is a low tunnel?
quiz.explanation: Low tunnels are made of hoops covered with plastic, providing frost protection.

quiz.q: How much can a high tunnel increase tomato yield per square meter?
quiz.explanation: A well-managed high tunnel can produce 8-10 kg per square meter, compared to 4-6 kg in open fields.
